summary: The last 4 weeks show a fragmented training block with very low swim volumes (mostly sub-2km sessions), inconsistent running, and a single long ride — all against a backdrop of chronically poor sleep (many nights under 5 hours) and depleted body battery readings that have frequently dropped below 30. The July 18th run at 179bpm average HR signals a significant overreach event, and the July 27–30 period (41 min sleep, body battery max of 5 and 2) indicates the athlete is entering the current week in a meaningful recovery deficit. With the Treviso 10K just 64 days away at a 5:45/km target, the priority must be rebuilding consistency and sleep hygiene before introducing any race-pace intensity.
suggestions: Protect sleep above all else for the next 2 weeks — without consistent 7h+ nights, no training adaptation will stick and the Treviso 10K target pace of 5:45/km will remain out of reach; consider enforcing a hard 10pm bedtime and eliminating evening screen exposure.

Introduce structured 10K-pace work gradually from Week 9 onward: start with 4x800m at 5:00–5:10/km as planned, then progress to 5x1km @ 5:45/km in Week 10 — this directly mirrors Treviso race demands without overstressing a system still in recovery.

Anchor at least two pool swims per week at 2,000m+ going forward; current open-water sessions of 300–2,000m are insufficient to build the technique base needed for Ironman Cervia and leave swim fitness stagnant.

Use the July 18th run (179bpm, 5:02/km) as a reference point: any run where HR exceeds 165bpm in the first 5 minutes should be immediately dialled back to 6:45/km — this is a clear pattern of going out too hard, which is compounding fatigue.

Monitor body battery each morning before every session over the next two weeks: if max body battery is below 35, convert any moderate or hard session to easy movement or full rest — the data from July 27–30 shows the cost of ignoring these signals.

proposed_changes.current_session: AI-adjusted pool swim: 30–40 min easy technique-only, 1,000–1,200m, drills at perceived effort only
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely — take full rest today. Body battery max was 2 on July 30th and sleep on July 27–30 averaged under 4 hours; even a light swim adds physiological load the body cannot absorb right now.
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery of 2 and near-zero sleep on July 27th indicate acute fatigue that makes even easy swimming counterproductive for adaptation today.

proposed_changes.current_session: AI-adjusted long run: 7–8km @ 7:00/km, HR ≤145bpm; convert to 30-min walk if HR exceeds 145bpm in first 2km
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with a 30-minute easy walk only — no running target. Confirm body battery is 50+ before starting; if below 50, rest completely.
proposed_changes.reason: Sleep debt from the July 27–30 period has not had sufficient days to clear, and attempting even a short run risks another high-HR overreach like July 18th.

proposed_changes.current_session: AI-adjusted 30-min easy run @ 6:45–7:00/km, HR ≤145bpm, flat route
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 30-min easy run @ 6:45–7:00/km, HR ≤145bpm as planned — but add a mandatory 5-min walk warm-up and abort if HR exceeds 150bpm before the 10-minute mark; log RPE alongside HR.
proposed_changes.reason: Adding the abort gate and RPE logging creates an objective checkpoint to confirm recovery is genuinely progressing before the Week 7 long run.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 4x800m @ 5:10–5:20/km with 2-min walk recovery between reps, total 35–40 min including warm-up and cool-down; only progress to the fourth rep if pace and HR feel controlled through rep 3.
proposed_changes.reason: Treviso target is 5:45/km so starting intervals at 5:10–5:20/km is more proportionate for a first quality session, reducing injury risk while still delivering useful race-pace stimulus 44 days out.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 5x1km @ 5:45/km (Treviso race pace) with 90-sec jog recovery, total 45–50 min including warm-up and cool-down; cap at 4 reps if HR exceeds 170bpm during any rep.
proposed_changes.reason: Shifting from sub-5:10/km pace to 5:45/km race-specific work 34 days before Treviso builds direct pace familiarity and reduces the risk of a pre-race injury from running significantly faster than goal pace.

proposed_changes.current_session: AI-adjusted 16km @ 6:30–6:45/km, 105–110 min; only extend if Aug 2nd run completed without issue and sleep improved to 7h+ average
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 12km @ 6:45/km, 80–85 min, flat route, HR strictly ≤145bpm throughout; walk the final 2km as cool-down. Do not attempt 16km unless body battery on waking exceeds 55 and the Aug 2nd session was a full run.
proposed_changes.reason: Given the acute recovery deficit entering this week, capping the Week 7 long run at 12km protects against a second overreach and keeps the Treviso build on track by arriving at Week 9 intervals healthy.
